title: Vishvamitra asks for Rama
hookLine: a king promises a sage anything, then hears what he wants
last: AVATAR: GOD COMES DOWN AS ONE OF US.

lines: A Well-known SAGE AT THE GATE.
cards: The four princes grow up learned, brave and close. Lakshmana sticks to Rama like a second shadow; Shatrughna to Bharata. Dasharatha, delighted, is already talking with his counselors about their weddings.
Then a guard rushes in: the sage Vishvamitra is at the gate.
Dasharatha hurries out, washes his feet, honors him, and says the words a king says to an honored guest, and maybe shouldn't: whatever you ask, consider it done. Vishvamitra smiles, and asks.

teach.b: Vishvamitra explains. He's begun a sacrifice, and two rakshasas, Maricha and Subahu, keep wrecking it, pouring blood and flesh on the altar. Under his vow he can't curse them in anger.
So he asks for Rama. Give me your eldest son, the boy who still wears a child's side-locks, for ten nights, to guard my rite. Dasharatha's world tilts.
He pleads, and Valmiki gives us his words: unashodasha-varsho me ramo rajivalochanah.
My lotus-eyed Rama is not yet sixteen. He's never fought. Take my army instead.
Take me. And when he hears who stands behind those two rakshasas, Ravana, he grows more frightened still. No, not Rama.
Now, Vishvamitra was born a king, and became a sage of the highest rank through fierce austerity. His name means friend of the whole world, but when a promise is taken back, his fire rises.
You're breaking your word, king, he says. Fine. I'll go as I came.
And the whole earth, the text says, trembles. Why would the earth shake over one sentence?
Because in Hinduism a word given is satya, truth, and Hindu texts name truthfulness again and again as part of dharma, the order that holds the world together.
A much later retelling in Awadhi, Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas, sums up the rule of Rama's family: life may go, but the word must not.
So Dasharatha stands between two things his tradition takes seriously: satya, and a father's love. The text doesn't call his fear wrong. Tomorrow, someone helps him choose.

how: Vishvamitra is honored in Hindu tradition as one of the great rishis; the Gayatri mantra of the Rig Veda is traditionally credited to him, and his request for Rama is told as the moment the prince's life of service begins.

o: the royal priest who raised Dasharatha's four sons
friend of the whole world: the king who became a sage
a rakshasa who wrecks a sage's fire sacrifice

games.q: at Dasharatha's gate — tap the pairs.
p: a king who became a sage
truth: a word given and kept

s: Vishvamitra was born a brahmin sage
he was born a king and became a brahmarshi through fierce austerity.
Dasharatha offers to fight the rakshasas himself
he offers his army, and himself, instead of Rama.
in the Ramayana, taking back a promise is a small thing
the earth itself trembles. a given word is satya, and truthfulness is part of dharma.

games.q: you're Dasharatha. you promised the sage anything, and he asks for your son. by the Ramayana's values, what's at stake?
o: your son, and satya: the word you gave.
nothing much; a king can change his mind.
games.why: he pleads that Rama isn't yet sixteen, and the earth trembles at the broken word. in the Ramayana a given word is satya, part of dharma.

practice: Before a puja or a vow, many Hindus make a sankalpa: they say plainly what they intend to do. Try a small one. Think of one promise you've made that has gotten heavier, to a child, a friend, yourself.

On the breath in, say it to yourself once, simply, the way a king's word was said at the gate. On the breath out, ask: can I keep it, and what would help? If you pray, offer it to God as a word you mean to keep.
If you don't, just hold it honestly.

wordCard.voice: Vishvamitra, friend of the whole world. The king-turned-sage asks Dasharatha for Rama, and a father's love meets a king's given word.

orig.note: Sanskrit viśvāmitra: viśva (all, the whole world) + mitra (friend).

carryVoice: Your line: a given word is satya. A father's fear, and a promise that shook the earth. See you tomorrow.
